decisions.reason: As an adjacent multi-item supplement range that likely costs little to maintain and supports the firm's consumer-health breadth, it remains worth keeping despite several years of learning.
Joint-health supplements fit the existing portfolio and pharmacy customer base, so unless sales have clearly disappointed the option value of keeping it is still higher than the modest carrying cost.

After several years the niche mushroom-based immune concept has likely revealed most of its potential, and in a large expanding portfolio management would reallocate resources from a still-uncertain peripheral supplement to stronger lines and new development.

The OTC migraine product is more resource-intensive than supplements but offers a strategic option in higher-value consumer medicines, so a growing pharmaceutical firm would usually keep it unless evidence is clearly weak.
